subject: Urgent: NimbleCart throughput spike & error surge — RCA + mitigation plan
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nimblecart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput drop + spike in 5xxs (NimbleCart prod)

Marcus / Jordan —

We started seeing a dramatic throughput degradation on our Redwood endpoints at ~06:35 UTC this morning. Requests are queuing and we're seeing a sustained 5xx rate of ~9-11% across our production region (us-west-2) since then. This is causing checkout failures for ~12% of sessions (we're seeing elevated abandonments on the cart flow).

What we've captured so far:
- Symptoms: request latency increased from median 120ms -> 650ms; 95th ~2.4s. 5xx rate jumped from 0.3% -> ~10%.
- Approx window: 06:35 UTC -> ongoing.
- Impact: loss of checkout revenue, customers are actively on support.

Attached are a small KPI snapshot and a short sample of logs when the error rate spiked. We need an RCA and mitigation plan ASAP — can we schedule an executive bridge and confirm who will lead the post-incident analysis?

Sophie
VP, Engineering — NimbleCart
Attachments: kpi_snapshot_20270925.csv (metrics), sample_request_traces.txt

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nimblecart.com>, Carlos Mejia <carlos.mejia@nimblecart.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + spike in 5xxs (NimbleCart prod)

Bridge summary and preliminary findings — 09:12 PT

Thanks all for jumping on the call. Quick summary of what we saw and immediate fixes: 

1) Incident timeline (observed by Redwood telemetry):
   - 06:33 UTC: a sudden increase in average request size (token count) for the NimbleCart baseline traffic — median tokens jumped ~3x for a subset of requests.
   - 06:34 UTC: our batching engine started to see longer queue times; autoscaling decisions lagged due to a burst of many small concurrent connections.
   - 06:35 UTC: backend GRPC pool hit a soft limit; requests began to return transient 503/504s while queueing increased.

2) Root causes (interim):
   - Primary: an upstream client change at NimbleCart expanded payload sizes for a small percent of traffic (unannounced), which increased per-request compute and changed our batching profile.
   - Secondary: autoscaler configuration for the dedicated pool was conservative for token-burst patterns; the fallback routing threshold to a lower-latency variant was not triggered due to a metric misconfiguration.

3) Immediate mitigations applied (within 20 minutes):
   - Enabled temporary traffic smoothing: accept fewer concurrent connections per worker to stabilize queues.
   - Forced routing for NimbleCart to the smaller M-L variant for new sessions (reduced per-request compute).
   - Increased GRPC worker pool and relaxed autoscale thresholds.

4) Customer-facing actions (what we told NimbleCart):
   - Quick rollback of client changes (Sophie confirmed they rolled back an experimental payload patch).
   - We implemented routing and autoscaler changes to restore baseline performance — observed error rate drop to ~0.6% after mitigations.

5) Follow-ups assigned (owners & ETA):
   - Jordan: full RCA write-up and post-incident playbook patches — due 2027-09-30 EOD.
   - Marcus: coordinate exec summary and financial impact estimate for NimbleCart — due 2027-10-01.
   - Grace: ops review to harden fallback/routing thresholds and autoscaler defaults across dedicated pools — plan due 2027-10-04.

Attached: short notes from the bridge and the sampling of traces. We will publish the formal RCA and a patch to the inference playbook by Thursday.

Jordan
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nimblecart.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: [CLOSED] NimbleCart incident: RCA, mitigations, and next steps

Sophie / Carlos / team —

Apologies for the delay; attached is the formal RCA packet (nimblecart_rca_20270930.pdf) and the playbook patch we applied to the inference routing engine (inference_playbook_patch.diff). High-level summary below: 

- Summary: Unannounced client-side payload growth combined with autoscaler sensitivity and a misconfigured fallback trigger led to queuing and transient 5xxs between 06:33–07:15 UTC on 2027-09-25.
- Impact: sustained elevated error rate peaked at 10.8%; estimated revenue impact (gross) for the window: $18k–$24k (Marcus will provide the exact estimate).
- Actions completed: temporary routing and autoscaler adjustments (25 Sep), rollback of client change (25 Sep), playbook patch deployed to all dedicated pools (29 Sep).
- Actions in flight:
   * Grace: update autoscale defaults + add regression test in CI for token-burst patterns (ETA 2027-10-04).
   * Jordan: add a Canary test that simulates token-burst traffic and validate fallback triggers (ETA 2027-10-01).
   * Marcus: negotiate a credit with NimbleCart for the window and deliver a commercial summary (ETA 2027-10-01).

Please find the full RCA attached and the link to the Jira ticket for tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1429. Let me know if you'd like us to schedule a short exec readout next week — Grace recommended a 15-minute briefing for NimbleCart leadership to review the corrective steps.

Thanks — and again, sorry for the disruption. We're running additional tests this week to ensure the fallback path behavior is deterministic under token-burst conditions.

Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: nimblecart_rca_20270930.pdf, inference_playbook_patch.diff
